business_scope.primary_industry_name: Cross-Border Physical Consignment of Shredded Non-Ferrous Scrap

Luxembourg-Germany Income Tax Treaty, as amended
Luxembourg-France Income Tax Treaty, as amended

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Loi modifiée du 12 novembre 2004 relative à la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme; Loi du 13 janvier 2019 instituant le Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE); Règlement grand-ducal du 12 mars 2019 relatif au RBE; Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales (Arts. 22-1 et seq. governing the SCSp); applicable CSSF Regulations, notably CSSF Regulation 12-02 on anti-money laundering and counter-terrorist financing.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Private_Internal (statutory restricted access; no unrestricted public search; access granted to competent authorities and professional AML/CFT obliged entities under Article 6 of the Law of 13 January 2019)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of passport or national identity document for each general partner, manager, and beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague Convention jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Original or certified copy of proof of residential address (recent utility bill or bank statement) for each principal individual
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public utility provider or regulated bank in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization, plus notarized signatory certification

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified extracts of commercial and beneficial ownership registers for any corporate general partner or shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registry of Commerce and Companies / UBO register in the corporate shareholder's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or certificate of no pending insolvency for any corporate general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry or court in the corporate general partner's home jurisdiction

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or source-of-funds letter covering initial capital and expected trade flows
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Regulated financial institution maintaining the relevant bank account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostilled or notarially certified signature by the issuing institution

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, managers, shareholders, UBOs, and counterparties against the consolidated lists of the Financial Action Task Force, United Nations Security Council sanctions, European Union restrictive measures, Luxembourg national lists, and internal enhanced-risk indicators; where transactions touch US correspondence banking, OFAC list screening is contractually required despite not being a Luxembourg domestic statutory obligation. Politically Exposed Person determination covers family members and close associates, with source-of-wealth/source-of-funds verification required for any PEP identified. Screening results must be documented in the AML/CFT file and refreshed every 180 days or upon material change.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company law filings are conducted in French, German, or Luxembourgish, with French predominant for the RCS. Corporate names must be expressed in Latin script. Non-Latin script names must be transliterated and, where necessary, accompanied by a certified French translation for all official registers.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In case of rejection, file a written re-examination request with the Luxembourg Business Registers within one month of refusal, specifying grounds of distinctiveness and non-confusion. If the registrar confirms the rejection, lodge an administrative appeal before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg within three months, with mandatory representation by a Luxembourg-admitted lawyer. A re-modified name can also be re-submitted at no additional statutory fee within the original reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable for substantive physical commodity trading activity. A bare virtual mailbox may satisfy formal RCS registration but will not support commercial substance, VAT registration, Luxembourg tax residency, beneficial ownership of accounts, or bank onboarding for documentary letters of credit. A physical managed office or a dedicated registered agent with appropriate operational oversight is required for this ISIC 4669 scope.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Medium-High: approximately 55% over a three-year operating horizon if engaged in recurrent VAT and income tax refund cycles; customs and AML/CFT desk-based compliance inspections raise the unannounced on-site probability to roughly 20% per audit event.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (Articles 16-1 to 16-19 governing the Société en Commandite Spéciale); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and on Accounting; Law of 2 September 2011 on Access to the Trades of Artisan, Merchant and Industrialist; Law of 21 March 2017 on Waste Management.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS (Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés), 2 boulevard Konrad Adenauer, L-1145 Luxembourg; online e-filing via www.lbr.lu.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Limited Partnership Agreement (Contrat de Société) executed by private writing (or by notarial deed if real property is contributed) together with the RCS electronic registration form (e-Form for SCSp).
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital for an SCSp; contributions may be in cash or in kind, fixed freely in the partnership agreement; cash contributions must be credited to a Luxembourg bank account in the partnership's name; in-kind contributions require a valuation annex; notarial deed is mandatory only if real property is contributed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: IN WRITING OF THE GENERAL PARTNER OF [•] SCSp: The undersigned, acting as General Partner of [•] SCSp (the 'Partnership'), adopts this First Resolution pursuant to Article 16-1 of the Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915, as amended. RESOLVED, that the Partnership's initial capital contribution is hereby subscribed and accepted; that the registered office is fixed at [address], Luxembourg; that [Name] be and hereby is appointed General Partner and Manager, authorised singly to bind the Partnership regarding wholesale trading of recycled copper scrap (ISIC 4669); that the RCS incorporation filing and RESA publication be approved; and that all officers are authorised to open bank accounts, obtain VAT/EORI numbers, and procure all regulatory licences. Adopted effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Execution of SCSp Limited Partnership Agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Notary (optional, mandatory only for real-property contributions) together with the founding partners; deed may be in English, French or German, with certified translation where required.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the partnership agreement containing: SCSp legal-form election, corporate name, registered office address in Luxembourg, duration, corporate object limited to wholesale trade in recycled non-ferrous scrap (ISIC 4669), identities and contributions of the General Partner and each Limited Partner, capital accounts, profit-sharing ratios, transfer restrictions, and the fiscal pass-through clause. Where the General Partner is not EU-resident, appoint a Luxembourg-resident agent for service of process. Execute by wet-ink or qualified electronic signature. If real property is contributed, execute before a Luxembourg notary and record the deed.
required_dossiers: Draft limited partnership agreement (original plus two copies)
Certified copies of passports or national IDs of General Partner and all Limited Partners
Proof of registered office address (lease agreement or domiciliation letter from a Luxembourg service provider)
Bank confirmation of initial cash contribution credited to the partnership account (if any)
Notarial deed or notarial attestation (if real property contribution)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a defect is identified, execute a supplementary amendment (avenant) signed by all partners; where notarization is required, the notary will issue a rectificatory deed before any RCS filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), RCS Department - online e-filing platform at www.lbr.lu.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the LBR e-filing portal using the representative's Luxtrust or elsh eID or the notary's account; select the SCSp incorporation e-Form; upload the signed PDF partnership agreement and a certified French or German translation if the deed is in English; complete standardized fields covering name, legal form, registered office, object (NACE 4669), partner data, contributions and General Partner powers; pay the EUR 75 statutory filing fee (approx. USD 82) online; track the application until the RCS registrar issues the numeric RCS registration number and the official extract (extrait).
required_dossiers: Signed partnership agreement (PDF upload)
Certified translation into French or German (if applicable)
LBR e-Form duly completed and digitally signed
Criminal record extract (casier judiciaire) of the General Partner if a natural person, or legal-entity excerpt if corporate General Partner
Non-bankruptcy declaration (déclaration de non-faillite) of the General Partner and Manager
Power of attorney for the filing representative (if not a partner)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a query or refusal, respond within the statutory 15-day period with the required rectification or additional documents; if the refusal stands, appeal to the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg within 3 months; most queries are cured by re-filing a corrected e-Form.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Official Electronic Gazette (RESA) and Third-Party Effect
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS / RESA - Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations, published by Luxembourg Business Registers.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS registration, the registry automatically drafts and publishes the legal notice in RESA summarizing identity, legal form, object, registered office, contributions, General Partner powers and financial year end. The SCSp obtains third-party effectiveness (opposabilité) of its registration only as of the RESA publication date. Download and archive the RESA publication PDF and the RCS extract, which are required by banks, insurers and counterparties for documentary letters of credit and SWIFT TT payment arrangements.
required_dossiers: RCS registration number
Verified data of the partnership (no separate submission required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA notice differs from the deed, submit a correction request to the RCS no later than one month; the RCS will re-publish a corrigendum; failure to publish timely may suspend the limited liability protection for Limited Partners.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT and EORI Registration for Intra-EU Trade
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des douanes et accises (AD&A) for EORI.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit VAT registration form (formulaire 700) to the AEDT electronically via MyGuichet, identifying the SCSp by RCS number and declaring activity code 4669 (wholesale of waste and scrap); state that non-EU counterparty transactions will apply the reverse-charge mechanism under Article 196 of EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC; apply simultaneously for the EORI number from the AD&A, mandatory for customs declarations of copper scrap imports into or exports out of the EU; appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative where the General Partner is non-EU resident.
required_dossiers: Form 700 (VAT registration), and Form 701 for joint VAT liability if applicable
RCS extract dated less than 3 months
Limited partnership agreement (certified copy)
Identification documents and tax IDs of the General Partner and Limited Partners
EORI application form (AD&A)
Power of attorney appointing Luxembourg VAT representative (if required)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the AEDT queries taxable person status, file a written explanation with the partnership's tax transparency ruling reference (election under Article 175bis LIR); late VAT registration may be regularized through the voluntary disclosure mechanism under Article 86 of the Luxembourg General Tax Law before penalties accrue.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie - Direction générale des Classes moyennes (Ministry of the Economy, General Directorate for Middle Classes), Luxembourg.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within a maximum of 15 days after formation, the General Partner as manager must apply for the business establishment permit for the commercial activity of wholesale trade in waste and scrap (NACE 4669). The natural-person manager must prove a Luxembourg-recognized diploma or at least 10 years of professional experience in the metals trading sector, have no criminal record, no bankruptcy history, and Luxembourg residence or a resident professional representative. Attach the management mandate, insurance certificates and lease of the registered office. The permit is personal to the SCSp and limits the operator to the declared activity exclusively.
required_dossiers: Autorisation d'établissement application e-form via MyGuichet
Criminal record certificate of the Manager/General Partner issued within 3 months
Diploma or professional experience certificate proving qualification for wholesale metals trade
Proof of residence and ID of the Manager
RCS extract and partnership agreement
Civil liability insurance certificate
Statement of non-bankruptcy
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: In case of refusal, appeal to the Administrative Tribunal within 3 months; alternatively complete missing professional qualifications by requesting equivalence (reconnaissance de qualification) from the Ministry of Education and re-apply; a temporary declaration of exercise may be filed to preserve the application timeline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Waste Dealer and Broker Authorization under Environmental Law
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'Environnement (Luxembourg Environment Agency) under the Minister of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the waste dealer/broker authorization application (autorisation de négociant/courtier en déchets) with the Administration de l'Environnement, designating the SCSp as dealer/broker in non-hazardous waste destined for recycling. Submit a waste management plan listing EWC codes 17 04 01 (copper, bronze, brass), 17 04 07 (mixed non-ferrous metals) and 20 01 40 (metals), identifying certified upstream suppliers and downstream recycling operators within the EU, and describing any interim storage arrangements. If storage exceeds 50 tonnes of non-hazardous waste, the storage site becomes classified under the Law of 21 March 2017 and requires a notification or communal authorization with site plan, sealed floor, fire detection and retention tank; provide a financial guarantee where applicable. The authorization is personal to the SCSp and must be renewed upon any change of General Partner or business address.
required_dossiers: Waste dealer authorization application form (ADR/AED)
RCS extract and valid autorisation d'établissement
Waste management plan with EWC code list (17 04 01; 17 04 07; 20 01 40)
Certificates of registered downstream recycling facilities in the EU (ISO 14001 or national waste permit)
Site plan and technical description of storage premises (if any)
Financial guarantee certificate if storage capacity is equal to or greater than 50 tonnes
Environmental damage civil liability insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is objected to, submit missing technical data within 30 days; upon informal refusal, request the Minister's internal review and thereafter appeal to the Administrative Tribunal within 3 months from notification; no waste trading activity may be performed before the authorization is granted.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy - General Directorate for Middle Classes (business establishment permit) jointly with the Administration de l'Environnement (waste dealer/broker authorization); workplace supervision by the Labour and Mines Inspectorate (ITM).
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit for Wholesale Trade in Waste and Scrap, NACE 4669) and Autorisation de négociant/courtier en déchets (Waste Dealer/Broker Authorization) under the Law of 21 March 2017 on Waste Management.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement - Luxembourg Environment Agency, Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Sustainable Development
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Trading and brokerage of scrap metals is not an Annex I or II activity under the Luxembourg EIA Law of 15 May 2018; a full EIA is not required. The operation falls under Category 2 (notification/declaration) of the Law of 21 March 2017: a waste dealer authorization is mandatory; if interim storage exceeds 50 tonnes of non-hazardous waste, the storage site is a classified waste facility requiring a separate authorization with prior environmental inspection. Full EIA (Category 1) would apply only to a copper smelting/refining or shredding facility, which is outside the licensed trading scope.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: The pure trading and consignment model generates no process wastewater, no VOCs and no stack emissions. For interim storage of shredded copper wire, the operator must comply with: sealed impermeable flooring with liquid-tight drainage routed to a retention tank; stormwater and wash-water discharge thresholds under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 10 July 2018 on industrial wastewater and EU Directive 2000/60/EC; dust control by mobile water spraying where particulate matter approaches the limit values of Directive 2008/50/EC; and prohibition of open burning of insulation residues, with any rejected PVC insulation consigned as hazardous waste EWC 17 04 02 to an authorized treatment facility.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS) for any storage premises, including fire separation distances for metal stacking, smoke detectors and extinguishers; structural certificate from a recognized engineering office validating the load-bearing capacity of floors and racks under the Eurocodes; occupational clearance from the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering the workplace risk assessment under Article L.312-1 of the Labour Code, provision of PPE (gloves, safety boots, eye protection) for handling shredded copper wire, noise exposure limits under the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 7 October 2009 implementing Directive 2003/10/EC, and periodic inspection of lifting and handling equipment.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; portal: MyGuichet.lu / rcs.lu
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Register the SCSp with the Luxembourg Business Register (RCS) to obtain the business registration number (numéro d'immatriculation). The SCSp, having no legal personality, is entered as a fiscally transparent partnership. Apply to the AEDT for a VAT identification number (format LU + 8 digits) using the simplified registration form for non-resident entities; non-established foreign traders may appoint a Luxembourg fiscal representative for VAT procedures. The direct tax TIN for individual and corporate partners is assigned by the ACD; no separate tax ID is issued to the SCSp for income tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Tax transparency is mandatory for the SCSp under Luxembourg domestic law; no check-the-box election exists. Available statutory options include VAT grouping (assujetti unique), fiscal unity for corporate income tax if the entity were taxable, the 80% participation exemption regime for qualifying shareholdings held through the SCSp, and the notional interest deduction. Hybrid mismatch rules under ATAD 2 may impose a DTT-dependent reclassification if partners reside in jurisdictions that treat the SCSp as opaque.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 taxable turnover per annum for small undertakings established in Luxembourg; non-established foreign suppliers are subject to mandatory VAT registration without a turnover threshold. Intra-Community distance sales of goods to consumers trigger registration under the OSS regime once the EUR 10,000 EU-wide cross-border threshold is exceeded.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Luxembourg does not operate a continuous transaction control or real-time fiscal clearance system; no digital stamping or API-based clearance is currently imposed. B2B electronic invoicing is permitted, and B2G e-invoicing via PEPPOL/factur-X is mandatory for public sector contracts. VAT returns (RL) and EC Sales Lists must be filed electronically through the AEDT portal; export declarations are lodged via the e-Customs system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of recycled scrap copper wire to buyers outside the EU are zero-rated under Article 41 of the Luxembourg VAT Law provided the goods are physically exported to a third country and the supplier holds documentary proof of export within the prescribed period. Intra-EU supplies to a taxable counterparty are zero-rated as intra-Community supplies when the buyer provides a valid EU VAT identification number, the EC Sales List is filed, and transport evidence is retained. The zero-rating remains available even if the scrap is cut, shredded, or compacted in Luxembourg, provided no installation, assembly, or processing that destroys the commodity nature occurs before export.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (e-Customs EX summary declaration and export entry)
Bill of Lading or CMR consignment note with proof of physical departure from EU territory
Commercial invoice, packing list, and mandatory vehicle scale ticket or pre-shipment weight certificate for scrap metal
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT MT103 / Telegraphic Transfer credit confirmation evidencing payment receipt within the repatriation deadline
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Claims for export zero-rating are subject to declaration-level and documentary audit by the AEDT. Failure to produce conclusive export evidence within the statutory period triggers reassessment of the 17% VAT and default interest at 0.6% per month, plus administrative fines up to EUR 5,000 or higher in aggravated cases. Deliberate or fraudulent export misdeclaration attracts criminal sanctions under Article 102 of the VAT Law, including imprisonment up to four years and fines; VAT refunds already credited are clawed back with compound interest. Export records and underlying transport documents must be retained for at least ten years from the end of the year to which they relate.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) in coordination with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) and the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance; customs and excise controls are administered by the Administration des douanes et accises.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a full member of the Economic and Monetary Union and adopted the euro as its sole legal tender; there are no exchange controls on current or capital account transactions. Both capital flows and profit remittances are freely convertible, subject only to general EU sanctions screening, AML/KYC checks by resident credit institutions, and mandatory balance-of-payments statistical reporting to the BCL. Dividend and profit distributions by an SCSp to foreign partners are unrestricted and are not subject to withholding tax at source, provided the entity is treated as fiscally transparent. No prior administrative authorization is required for cross-border transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory timelines or mandatory conversion ratios for export receipts under Luxembourg law. Export proceeds from recycled copper scrap sales may be retained in euros or foreign currency accounts at any authorised credit institution without surrender obligations to the BCL. The SCSp must, however, report all cross-border payments exceeding EUR 12,500 to the BCL for balance-of-payments statistics within the applicable monthly reporting window, and must comply with EU sanctions and cash-control regulations where physical cash is involved.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (Spuerkeess)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low. Offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs) that hold neither a Luxembourg licence nor a valid EU passport under PSD2 are not permitted to provide payment accounts to a Luxembourg-resident SCSp. The CSSF requires any EMI offering services in Luxembourg to be authorised or passported; non-EU fintechs face significant legal barriers. Even where passporting exists, most digital EMIs do not support documentary credit operations, commodity trade settlement, or the high-limit SWIFT transactions required for this trading scope. The SCSp should rely exclusively on tier-1 banks for core treasury functions; an EMI may be used only as a supplementary low-balance expense rail.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is the prevailing norm. Luxembourg credit institutions normally require at least the general partner's authorised signatories and the ultimate beneficial owners to attend an in-person onboarding meeting at the bank's registered office or a recognised foreign branch; fully remote account opening is rarely granted for a commodity-trading SCSp classified as Medium_Risk_Enhanced. Where remote video identification is accepted, it is subject to CSSF-compliant e-IDAS-certified electronic identification, and the bank retains the right to demand a subsequent physical interview. Certified copies of the partnership agreement, the RBE (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs) extract, and notarised board resolutions must be produced.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Intangible ownership structure of the SCSp, including foreign limited partners with indirect control
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Duly filed RBE extract, full ownership chain diagrams, partnership agreement and private placement memorandum, LEI certificate, notarised identification documents of each ultimate beneficial owner, and sworn statements confirming source of funds and source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Commodity trading classification as Medium_Risk_Enhanced, particularly physical circular-metal consignments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete transaction dossier comprising purchase contracts, commercial invoices, bills of lading, weightbridge certificates, supplier recycling licences, customs declarations, and the SCSp's documented AML/CTF procedures under Luxembourg law of 12 November 2004, as amended.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Counterparty jurisdiction exposure in emerging-market scrap supply chains
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Sanctions screening results (EU/UN consolidated lists), country risk assessment memorandum, passport and corporate registry extracts of counterparties, end-user declarations, and third-party due diligence reports from reputable KYC providers.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Insufficient economic substance of the SCSp in Luxembourg
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Local substance dossier evidencing registered office in Luxembourg, physically present general partner or locally appointed authorised manager, local bank account, Luxembourg bookkeeping service provider, and tax compliance history demonstrating the partnership's operative reality.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Absence of audited financial statements in early-stage treasury operations
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Interim management accounts prepared by an approved Luxembourg chartered accountant (réviseur d'entreprises), projected cash flow schedule, capital contribution proof, and a sworn escrow arrangement letter from the receiving bank.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Capital contributions must be routed through the general partner's bank account or directly into the SCSp's segregated capital escrow account at a CSSF-licensed credit institution via SEPA (EUR) or SWIFT MT103 (non-EUR). The payment instruction must reference the SCSp LEI and the specific contribution clause of the partnership agreement, and the respective partner must complete the bank's source-of-funds declaration. For balance-of-payments accuracy, purpose code 601 (direct investment) should be used where applicable. Any contribution exceeding EUR 12,500 must be included in the BCL statistical return. No exchange control approval is required, but the receiving bank will verify the RBE filing and confirm that no sanctioned persons are involved.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Operational disbursements for recycled copper scrap purchases are settled primarily through SWIFT MT103/MT202 payments and documentary credit instruments. Recommended rails: (a) irrevocable confirmed commercial letters of credit issued under UCP 600 with a Luxembourg or EU confirming bank for large consignments; (b) documentary collections (D/P and D/A) for mid-sized transactions; and (c) direct SWIFT TT with full shipping documents exchanged against payment for small recurring shipments. All outbound payments must carry accurate EU Combined Nomenclature classification, customs export declarations, and the SCSp's VAT number where intra-community acquisitions apply. Payment routing must preserve the chain of title from supplier to the SCSp and onward to the end buyer, with each leg documented to satisfy the Medium_Risk_Enhanced compliance profile.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD outright forward contracts with a CSSF-licensed or EEA-passported credit institution
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) priced against restricted or non-convertible settlement currencies
Cross-currency swaps between EUR and major trade settlement currencies (USD, CNY, GBP)
Commodity-indexed swap structures referencing LME copper and scrap-price benchmarks where the underlying physical exposure is documented

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Confirmation (Confirmation annuelle) of RCS data - periodic validation of SCSp identity, registered office, managing general partner, and activity codes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Mandatory every calendar year between 1 January and 30 September; the filing window is calendar-year based and independent of the incorporation or financial-year anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing after 30 September triggers an increased administrative processing fee and formal reminder; persistent default empowers the Registrar to petition the Luxembourg District Court for a coercive fine (astreinte), and the Public Prosecutor may seek judicial dissolution/strike-off of the SCSp

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Declaration (Déclaration des bénéficiaires effectifs) - registration and annual no-change corroboration with the RBE
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of incorporation and within one month of any transfer or change of partnership interests; no separate UBO annual return exists, but the LBR annual confirmation in the January-September window operates as the annual confirmation that UBO data has not changed
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file or update within the one-month legal deadline is a criminal offence punishable by fines of EUR 250 to EUR 250,000 for legal persons and imprisonment of six months to five years for individuals, in addition to RCS strike-off risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Luxembourg VAT Return and Annual Recapitulative Declaration (form 5001 annual annex) - applicable because the SCSp conducts physical consignment trading activities
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual recapitulative VAT return due by 1 May of the following calendar year; monthly or quarterly periodic VAT returns remain due by the 15th of the following month or quarter
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing draws automatic late-payment interest at 0.6% per month and a per-return fine of EUR 250 to EUR 1,000; wilful non-declaration can lead to criminal prosecution of the managing general partner and VAT recovery enforcement

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: None at entity level: the SCSp is exempt from the statutory legal audit because it has no legal personality; statutory audit applies only if the SCSp is constituted as a regulated reserved alternative investment fund (RAIF/SIF) under CSSF supervision or if the partnership agreement expressly requires a Luxembourg réviseur d'entreprises
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: No obligation to prepare or publish statutory annual accounts under the Law of 19 December 2002; internal books are nevertheless maintained under Luxembourg GAAP (Plan comptable luxembourgeois) with IFRS-based schedules prepared for institutional partners, and VAT records must comply with AEDT invoicing rules

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp must maintain an internal UBO register and file the UBO declaration with the LBR within one month of incorporation and within one month of every change in beneficial ownership; transfers of partnership interests must first be inscribed in the SCSp's statutorily required register of partners (Registre des associés) to be opposable, after which the corporate agent re-validates the UBO schedule and records a no-change certification during the annual RCS confirmation window
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Registre des associés of the SCSp)
Minute Book (Resolutions of partners and managing general partner)
Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 3,000 - USD 6,000 per annum for a Luxembourg professional support service (PFS) covering registered office, AML/KYC utility, corporate secretarial support, annual confirmation filing, and UBO register maintenance
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not legally required for the SCSp; voluntary certified audit or agreed-upon procedures engagements are typically quoted at USD 15,000 - USD 35,000 for a mid-sized physical commodities trading SCSp

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 0% at the SCSp level because the SCSp is fiscally transparent and has no Luxembourg corporate income tax liability; for ordinary resident corporations the aggregate headline CIT rate in Luxembourg City is 24.94% (17% IRC + 7% unemployment solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp benefits from full tax transparency: no Luxembourg CIT, municipal business tax, or net wealth tax at the partnership level. Income is taxed directly at the partner level. Corporate partners holding qualifying participations may benefit from the Luxembourg participation exemption (100% exemption on dividends and capital gains), provided the 10% or EUR 6 million threshold and 12-month holding period are satisfied. No Luxembourg tax holiday applies to an SCSp, and the entity-level tax rate is nil.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited for qualifying corporate taxpayers under Luxembourg domestic law; in an SCSp, losses are not retained at the entity level but passed through to partners subject to the partners' own tax residence rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Unified tax declaration filed via MyGuichet.lu/eCDF; SCSp files an informational tax declaration confirming tax transparency, while each partner files its own income tax return (Form 100 for individuals, Form 520 for corporate partners).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year SCSp, the informational declaration is due by 31 March of the following tax year, extended to 31 May if filed electronically; for a non-calendar accounting year, the return is due within six months of the accounting close.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Entity identification: name, RCS registration number, Luxembourg tax matricule, and registered office address.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The foreign general partner must additionally provide its own foreign entity identifier and tax residence details when it is the filer or authorized manager.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal form classification: Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp), fiscal transparency election / statutory transparency status.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter SCSp and state clearly that the entity is not liable to Luxembourg corporate income tax, municipal business tax, or net wealth tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Accounting period start and end dates; assumed tax year or financial year, consistent with RCS annual accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Use the financial year adopted by the general partner in the limited partnership agreement; amend by RCS publication if changed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Partner schedule: full names, residence addresses, profit-sharing percentages, and country of tax residence for all partners.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign partners must enter their tax residence country; attach a valid Tax Residence Certificate where treaty protection is claimed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Material declaration of zero taxable income at the SCSp level, with a narrative describing the transparent treatment under Article 2 LIR.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not allocate or report Luxembourg-source taxable income in the SCSp return; income flows to partners under domestic and treaty rules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cross-border transactions summary: volume of scrap metal sales, purchase counterparties, payment rails, and related-party transaction list.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Indicate arm's-length remuneration and mention the method used where related-party trading occurred; this supports the TP documentation file.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing can trigger an administrative fine of up to EUR 1,500 and late-payment interest of 0.6% per month on any resulting tax liability; deliberately false declarations constitute tax fraud punishable by imprisonment of up to five years and fines up to EUR 12,500, plus restoration of the evaded tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% at the SCSp level because the SCSp is transparent and not a resident company. Distributions of profits to partners are not dividends for Luxembourg WHT purposes. If the same economic profit is later paid by a non-transparent Luxembourg resident company, the domestic dividend WHT rate is 15%, with treaty relief commonly reducing it to 0% to 5%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Because the SCSp does not levy WHT, a foreign partner generally needs no Luxembourg relief application. Where treaty protection is required for upstream payments derived through an opaque Luxembourg entity, the beneficial owner must submit a Tax Residence Certificate issued by the foreign competent authority, together with a Luxembourg withholding tax refund or relief-at-source application on the prescribed legal form; evidence of beneficial ownership, anti-abuse compliance, and satisfaction of any qualifying holding period must accompany the submission.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law imposes no withholding tax on interest or royalties paid by a Luxembourg entity to non-residents, subject to prescribed anti-abuse limitations. Tax treaties generally secure rates of 0% to 10%; most Luxembourg DTAs reduce royalty and interest WHT to 0%, while certain source-country residual taxes may apply under treaty safeguards.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_value: No explicit statutory Euro threshold is codified for the SCSp; the Luxembourg tax administration may request transfer pricing documentation on a case-by-case basis under Article 56bis LIR. Benchmark practices require a Local File where related-party transactions are commercially significant, especially for tangible cross-border trading above EUR 100,000 per annum, and a Master File if the LU partner belongs to an MNE group with consolidated turnover above EUR 50 million; CbCR filing applies where group revenue equals or exceeds EUR 750 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The formal Economic Substance Regulations of the Gulf jurisdictions do not apply in Luxembourg. However, the Luxembourg general anti-abuse rule (Article 6 LIR), the ATAD CFC rules, and the Principal Purpose Test under tax treaties require real economic activity. A pure conduit SCSp owning no people, premises, procurement function, or trading substance in its recycled copper scrap activity may be disregarded for treaty benefits, recharacterized, or exposed to penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately omitting profits from cross-border copper scrap sales, falsifying invoices, manufacturing artificial purchase costs, or failing to report attributable income to partners.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of all disguised income; monthly late-payment interest of 0.6%; administrative penalties up to EUR 12,500; in aggravated cases imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years; exclusion from public contracts in Luxembourg; publication of the conviction in commercial registers.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The general partner or manager who directed the fraud is jointly and severally civilly liable for the tax loss; criminal conviction can lead to imprisonment, prohibition from managing a commercial entity, weighing of assets for restitution, and seizure of passport/travel restrictions where a flight risk is established.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling recycled scrap copper wire at artificially depressed prices to a related offshore buyer with no arm's-length comparability, no contemporaneous TP file, and unexplained margin erosion.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Luxembourg tax administration recharacterizes the transaction under Article 56bis LIR and adjusts taxable income upward; penalty of up to 10% of the additional corporate tax due, plus 0.6% monthly interest; secondary tax may be imposed in the foreign buyer's jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly certified the distorted TP policy can be held civilly liable for the adjusted tax plus penalties; criminal referral for document falsification may trigger imprisonment, director disqualification, and personal attachment orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the SCSp as an invoicing shell with no office, no staff, no physical handling of scrap, no procurement records, no warehouse, and no decision-making in Luxembourg.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Application of Article 6 LIR GAAR and Treaty Shopping defenses; denial of Luxembourg tax residency certificates; denial of treaty benefits under the MLI principal purpose test; reallocation of profits to the ultimate parent; liquidation of the entity may be forced by RCS; administrative fines and costs assessed.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The General Partner is exposed under the SCSp partnership agreement and civil law to unlimited liability for partnership debts if the entity is found to be fictitious; shareholders or managers may be ordered to repay diverted profits; criminal liability arises where the shell was used to commit fraud, papers can be seized, and a travel ban may be issued during criminal investigations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to perform customer due diligence and beneficial ownership verification on scrap suppliers or buyers; accepting large cash or bearer instruments; trading in copper wire sourced from sanctioned jurisdictions or conflict zones without chain-of-custody records.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Breach of Luxembourg AML laws (Law of 12 November 2004 as amended and EU Directives) carries administrative fines up to EUR 5 million or twice the economic benefit recovered; sanctions violations trigger asset freeze and criminal penalties of up to EUR 1 million and imprisonment of 1 to 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: AML duties apply to beneficial owners and managing partners individually; culpable directors can be disqualified from managing financial or commercial entities, ordered to pay restitution, subjected to monitoring by the CAA, and, in serious proceedings, remanded in custody with a travel ban imposed.
